compiled_state.description:
## Discovered from

rebar-debug on bug `masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle` (3a52-2d79-320d-4fed), root cause RC-A. See
that ticket's "Phase 1 EXIT" comment for the full evidence trail.

## Problem

`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:99` calls `materialize_tickets(...)` on every attested gate
resolution. `materialize_tickets` (`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:675-703`)
content-addresses the entry as `<store>/tickets-<sha>` and builds it with `_materialize_tree`
(`:373-410`, `git read-tree` + `git checkout-index`) — every file written fresh, with no
hardlinking, no delta against a neighbouring entry, and no per-review release
(`SnapshotHandle._cleanup` at `:199` is never assigned by any producer).

The key is the live tickets-branch tip: `_pin_tickets_sha` (`:534-609`) resolves the tracker
via `config.tracker_dir()`, and `tracker_dir_override()` (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:65-79`)
returns `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` verbatim.

Measured on `origin/tickets`:

- **69,984 blobs**, ≈620 MiB (~800 MiB allocated). The code snapshot alongside it is
  41.6 MiB / 3,131 files — **15x smaller**.
- **1,374 commits** in a 10-hour window (2026-08-17 18:00 → 2026-08-18 04:00 PDT): the tip
  moves every ~26 seconds.
- each of the last 5 consecutive tickets commits changed **exactly 1 file**.

So a one-file delta produces a fresh 620 MiB copy — roughly 10^5x write amplification — on a
key with effectively **zero reuse**. The review-bot's own `code_review` artifact write
(`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: always`, `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:120`) guarantees the ref advances
between reviews even if nothing else in the fleet were writing.

On the review-bot host this modelled 2.5-10 GiB/h of root-disk growth; the measured rate during
the 2026-08-17 incident was 4.4 GiB/h.

## Why this is a defect

`docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md` D2 rests on "an immutable SHA is a perfect cache
key", which holds only for keys with **reuse**. This key has none, so the structure behaves as
an append-only log of full copies rather than the bounded, reclaimable cache the ADR describes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A review no longer writes a full copy of the ticket tree when the previous entry differs
      by a handful of files (hardlink/reflink against the prior entry, materialize only the
      paths the gate actually reads, or pin a coarser/stabler key) — with the chosen approach
      justified against ADR 0005's integrity guarantees.
- [ ] A test observes the amplification RED (N reviews across N adjacent tickets SHAs consume
      ~1 tree, not N trees) and GREEN after the repair.
- [ ] `materialize_tickets` participates in the store's byte accounting (see the sibling
      ticket) so the entries it creates are visible to any size-based reclaim.
- [ ] ADR 0005 / `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` updated to state the key-reuse assumption and how
      the tickets key satisfies it.
compiled_state.title: Gate snapshot store copies the whole ~620 MiB ticket tree per review on a cache key with no reuse
